clauses.part: Purpose of the insurance and policy period
clauses.text: The purpose of this insurance is to cover the coverages that the declarations page shows as contracted: civil liability to third parties, loss of the vehicle by damage or theft, medical expenses of the occupants and personal accident cover for the driver. Once the premium is paid, Autos Poblado pays them on the terms of this contract, for loss events that happen within the territory set out in the general conditions. A loss event is the occurrence that causes the damage or the loss. This insurance is voluntary and does not replace the SOAT.

clauses.part: Purpose of the insurance and policy period
clauses.text: Coverage runs for the policy period shown on the declarations page, as long as the premium is paid. Keeping it in force depends on the policyholder meeting the duties this contract assigns, especially those in the section "Duties after a loss event".

"You" means the policyholder, the person who bought the insurance and is listed as the insured on the declarations page. It also includes that person's spouse or permanent partner while the two share a home. The beneficiary of the payment for damage to the vehicle is you, unless the declarations page names someone else, such as a bank holding a pledge on the vehicle.
"We" means Autos Poblado, the insurer that issues this policy and stands behind it.
"Personal injury" means any harm to a person's health caused by the accident, including wounds, illness that follows from them and, when it happens, death.

"Property damage" means breaking, destroying or making unusable a physical object that belongs to a third party, such as another car, a fence or a storefront. A third party is anyone other than you, your spouse or permanent partner, and whoever drives with your permission.

"Covered auto" means the private passenger car listed on the declarations page. A vehicle you buy during the policy period is also a covered auto if you tell us about it within 20 days of taking delivery.

"Commercial value" means what your covered auto is worth on the market on the day of the loss event, according to the Fasecolda Value Guide. The guide is read with the vehicle's code and model year. The commercial value is the basis of the insured value.
"Family member" means someone who lives in your home and is related to you by birth, marriage, permanent partnership or adoption, including children in your legal care.
"Occupant" means someone inside a vehicle, climbing in or out of it, or standing next to it while loading it or pushing it by hand.

When you or an authorized driver cause, with the covered auto, a traffic accident for which they must answer to a third party under the law, Autos Poblado pays the damages for property damage, for death or injury to one person and for death or injury to two or more people. We pay up to the limits of this section and in excess of what the SOAT covers. An authorized driver is someone who drives with your permission and a valid driver's license. We also handle your defense against those claims with lawyers we choose, and we may settle with the victim whenever we think it wise. Our defense duty stops once our payments reach the limit.

In addition to the limit of this section, and without reducing it, we pay the costs of the lawsuit that the victim files against you or against us over a covered accident (Commercial Code, art. 1128), any court bond needed, and your reasonable out-of-pocket costs when we ask for help with the case, including travel to hearings and up to COP 120,000 for each day of work missed. We do not pay them if the accident was caused on purpose or is excluded, or if you face the lawsuit against our written instruction.
This section does not cover harm that you or an authorized driver cause on purpose, or harm someone else causes following your instructions.
This section does not cover damage to things you own or are carrying in the vehicle.
This section does not cover damage to things you have rented, borrowed or are looking after for someone else.
This section does not cover injuries to your own employees that happen while they are working; those are handled by the labor and occupational risk systems.

This section does not cover accidents that happen while the vehicle provides public transport service or carries people or goods for pay, including trips booked through a ride app. Friends splitting the cost of a trip is not considered pay.
This section does not cover liability that arises while the vehicle is used in a business that sells, repairs, washes, parks or stores vehicles.
This section does not cover anyone driving a vehicle without the owner's permission or without a sound reason to believe they had it.
This section does not cover accidents during races, speed contests or performance tests, or while practicing for them.
This section does not pay fines, traffic tickets, penalties or damages that a court imposes to punish rather than to repair harm.
This section does not cover driving a motorcycle, a motorized three-wheeler or any other two- or three-wheeled vehicle.
This section does not cover using a vehicle you own that is not listed on the declarations page, except a newly bought vehicle that the covered auto definition includes.
This section does not cover using a vehicle that a family member owns, or that a family member has on hand for regular use, unless that vehicle is listed on the declarations page.

The declarations page sets three limits. The limit for death or injury to one person is the most we pay for each victim in one accident. The limit for death or injury to two or more people is the most for all victims of that accident. The property damage limit is the most for all third-party property damaged. Adding insureds, vehicles or claims does not raise these limits.

When a territory endorsement extends the policy to another country and the law there requires compulsory insurance to drive, that insurance pays first and this section pays the excess, up to the limit on the declarations page. We never pay twice for the same loss.

This section does not replace the SOAT, which the law requires of every vehicle on the road. What the SOAT covers responds first, and this policy pays the excess, with at least the minimum limits set in the "Legal framework" document.

If another liability policy also responds to the accident, we split the payment in proportion to each policy's limits. For a vehicle you do not own, that vehicle's own insurance pays first and we pay what remains.

If you, the authorized driver or another occupant of the covered auto is injured in a traffic accident, Autos Poblado pays their reasonable medical, hospital and funeral expenses, in excess of what the SOAT covers. The expenses must arise within two years of the accident.
This section does not pay for injuries suffered on a motorcycle or any other two- or three-wheeled vehicle.
This section does not pay for injuries suffered while the vehicle provides public transport service or carries passengers for pay.
This section does not pay for injuries that happen while the vehicle is being used as a home or as a fixed workplace.
This section does not pay for injuries suffered in races, speed contests or performance tests.
The per-person limit on the declarations page is the most we pay toward each injured occupant's medical costs from one accident, however many people or vehicles are involved.
If the SOAT or another medical expenses policy covers the same costs, we pay only what is left unpaid after it, up to our limit.

clauses.part: Personal accident cover for the driver
clauses.text: If the authorized driver of the covered auto dies, or is left with a permanent disability, because of a traffic accident that happens while driving, Autos Poblado pays the personal accident insured value shown on the declarations page. For a permanent disability we pay according to the percentage of lost capacity determined by the competent authority. If the driver dies, we pay the driver's beneficiaries.

clauses.part: Personal accident cover for the driver
clauses.text: This section does not cover an accident of the driver while driving a vehicle that is not the covered auto.

clauses.part: Personal accident cover for the driver
clauses.text: This section does not cover death or disability that the driver causes to themselves on purpose.

clauses.part: Personal accident cover for the driver
clauses.text: This section does not apply while the vehicle provides public transport service or carries people or goods for pay.

clauses.part: Personal accident cover for the driver
clauses.text: This section does not cover anyone driving the vehicle without the owner's permission or without a sound reason to believe they had it.

clauses.part: Personal accident cover for the driver
clauses.text: The most we pay under this section is the personal accident insured value shown on the declarations page, once per accident, however many vehicles or people are involved. What the at-fault party pays the victim is not subtracted.

clauses.part: Personal accident cover for the driver
clauses.text: If the driver has other personal accident insurance, each policy pays its own insured value: what the others pay does not reduce what we pay.

clauses.part: Personal accident cover for the driver
clauses.text: If we disagree with you or the beneficiaries about whether a payment is owed, about the degree of disability or about the amount, either side may ask for the question to be decided by a single arbitrator in Colombia. Each side pays its own costs and half of the arbitrator's fee.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: Autos Poblado pays for damage to the covered auto if you collide with another vehicle or an object, or if the vehicle rolls over, even if you caused the crash. It also pays for damage from fire, flood, hail, falling objects, vandalism, broken glass or hitting an animal. In a partial loss, you pay the partial-loss-by-damage deductible on the declarations page: the deductible is the share of the loss that you bear.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: We also pay for theft of the covered auto, minus the partial-loss-by-theft deductible on the declarations page. It is a total loss by theft if the vehicle disappears and does not turn up after the report, and a partial loss by theft if parts or accessories are stolen.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: If your covered auto suffers a total loss by damage or theft, we reimburse what you spend getting around in the meantime, up to COP 60,000 a day and COP 1,800,000 in total, which is 30 days. Reimbursement starts on the third day after the loss event.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover damage that happens while the vehicle provides public transport service or carries people or goods for pay.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover wear from use, rust, lack of maintenance, or mechanical or electrical failure, unless it results from a theft or another covered loss.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover sound systems, screens, navigation units or other electronics that were not installed at the factory.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover personal belongings inside the vehicle, such as clothing, tools, cash or phones.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover damage limited to the tires, such as flats or blowouts, unless it comes from fire, theft or vandalism.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover losing the vehicle to seizure, impoundment or destruction ordered by an authority.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover damage caused by war, rebellion, organized terrorism or nuclear energy.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover damage suffered in races, speed contests or performance tests, or while practicing for them.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover parts, accessories or modifications added to the vehicle without telling us, such as custom wheels, altered suspension or engine upgrades.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover damage that you or a family member cause to the vehicle on purpose.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover damage caused by loading the vehicle beyond the weight its manufacturer allows.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover theft when the vehicle was left unlocked with the keys inside or with the engine running in a public place.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This section does not cover flood damage when the driver entered a road that authorities had closed or marked as flooded.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: The most we pay for a loss event is the insured value, which is the vehicle's commercial value in the Fasecolda Value Guide on the date of the loss event. If repairing the vehicle costs 75% or more of that value, it is a total loss. If it costs less, it is a partial loss and we pay the repair or the replacement of the parts with equivalent ones.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: We choose whether to pay the loss in cash or to arrange the repair or replacement ourselves. We pay within one month of the day you prove the loss event and its amount (Commercial Code, art. 1080). If the loss is total, the vehicle or what remains of it, which is the salvage, becomes ours and you sign the transfer. If a stolen vehicle turns up before we pay, we give it back to you and pay for any damage it suffered.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: This coverage does not benefit anyone who has the vehicle in their care as a business, such as a repair shop, a parking garage or a car transport company; if they caused the damage, we may recover it from them.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: If another policy or source covers the same loss, we pay only our share, in proportion to our limit against the total.

clauses.part: Loss of the vehicle by damage and by theft
clauses.text: If we and you disagree on the amount of a loss, each side names an appraiser and the two appraisers choose a third. What any two of the three agree on binds both sides. Each side pays its own appraiser and half of the third.
Tell us about the loss event within three business days of learning about it, as the legal framework sets (Commercial Code, art. 1075).
Tell us how, when and where it happened, and which vehicles and people were involved.
Give us the name and a way to reach any injured person and any witness you know of.
Work with us as we look into the claim and as we defend any claim made against you.
Send us right away a copy of any notice, summons or lawsuit you receive about the loss event, including a summons to a conciliation hearing.
If the claim involves injuries, attend the medical exams we request, with doctors we pay for, as often as is reasonable.

Give us the evidence that the loss event happened and what it cost (Commercial Code, art. 1077), a written account of the loss if we ask for one, and your authorization to obtain your medical records if there were injuries.
If the accident leaves injured or dead people, or the vehicle at fault drove off without being identified, tell the traffic authority within 24 hours and ask for the accident report.
Do not admit liability, settle or pay anything to the third party without our written authorization.
Take reasonable steps to keep the vehicle from further damage (Commercial Code, art. 1074); we pay back what you spend doing so.
If the vehicle or any of its parts was stolen, report it to the competent authority immediately.
Let us see and appraise the vehicle before you repair it or get rid of it.
If you become insolvent, Autos Poblado still owes what this policy covers. For civil liability, the payment is for the victim (Commercial Code, art. 1127).

This contract changes only in writing, through an endorsement we issue. You tell us in writing about any change that alters the risk, such as a change in how the vehicle is used, and we adjust the premium from the date of the change. Notices are sent to the address or email you gave us.

You described the state of the risk when buying the policy, and you must have done so truthfully. We give no coverage to anyone who knowingly lied about or hid an important fact about the accident, the loss or the state of the risk; if the inaccuracy was in good faith, the payment may be reduced as the law provides (Commercial Code, art. 1058).
The rights arising from this policy expire within the periods the law sets (Commercial Code, art. 1081), and no one may sue without first meeting the duties the policy sets.

When we pay for harm that someone else caused, we take your place to collect what we paid from that person, up to that amount (Commercial Code, art. 1096). You help us do so and do nothing to undermine it.

The policy covers loss events that happen during the policy period shown on the declarations page and within the territory of Colombia. There is no coverage outside Colombia unless a territory endorsement extends it to another country.

You may revoke the policy at any time by telling us in writing. We may revoke it only with the advance notice the legal framework requires, and we refund the premium for the time that had not yet run. If the premium is not paid on time, the policy ends automatically (Commercial Code, art. 1068).
If you sell the covered auto, or transfer your rights under this policy, the insurance does not pass to the buyer or to anyone else without our written consent.
If two or more insurances cover the same loss event, you must tell us about all of them. If they are Autos Poblado policies, the most we pay is the highest limit of any single one of them.
